arxiv-2201-03299.title: Avoiding Overfitting: A Survey on Regularization Methods for Convolutional Neural Networks Conference: Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection; June 03–05, 2018; Woodstock, NY Woodstock ’18: ACM Symposium on Neural Gaze Detection, June 03–05, 2018, Woodstock, NY Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.11
arxiv-2201-03299.creator: Claudio Filipi Gonçalves dos Santos, João Paulo Papa
arxiv-2201-03299.description: Abstract . Several image processing tasks, such as image classification and object detection, have been significantly improved using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). Like ResNet and EfficientNet, many architectures have achieved outstanding results in at least one dataset by the time of their creation. A critical factor in training concerns the network’s regularization, which prevents the structure from overfitting.

arxiv-2302-00942.title: Efficient Graph Field Integrators Meet Point Clouds
arxiv-2302-00942.creator: Krzysztof Choromanski, Arijit Sehanobish, Han Lin, Yunfan Zhao, Eli Berger, Tetiana Parshakova, Alvin Pan, David Watkins, Tianyi Zhang, Valerii Likhosherstov, Somnath Basu Roy Chowdhury, Avinava Dubey, Deepali Jain, Tamas Sarlos, Snigdha Chaturvedi, Adrian Weller
arxiv-2302-00942.description: Abstract We present two new classes of algorithms for efficient field integration on graphs encoding point clouds. The first class, SeparatorFactorization \mathrm{SeparatorFactorization} ( SF \mathrm{SF} ), leverages the bounded genus of point cloud mesh graphs, while the second class, RFDiffusion \mathrm{RFDiffusion} ( RFD \mathrm{RFD} ), uses popular ϵ \epsilon -nearest-neighbor graph representations for point clouds.

arxiv-2307-08374.title: Probing topology in nonlinear topological materials using numerical K K -theory
arxiv-2307-08374.creator: Stephan Wong, Terry A. Loring, Alexander Cerjan
arxiv-2307-08374.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Stephan Wong, Terry A. Loring, Alexander Cerjan. Nonlinear topological insulators have garnered substantial recent attention as they have both enabled the discovery of new physics due to interparticle interactions, and may have applications in photonic devices such as topological lasers and frequency combs. However, due to the local nature of nonlinearities, previous attempts to classify the topology of nonlinear systems have required significant approximations that must be tailored to individual systems.

arxiv-2410-11726.title: Robust control of Z-source inverter operated BLDC motor using Sliding Mode Control for Electric Vehicle applications
arxiv-2410-11726.creator: Gourab Das (Student Member, IEEE), Dibakar Das, Md Arif, Biplab Satpati
arxiv-2410-11726.description: Abstract The rapid development and expansion of the EV market marked by the advent of third decade of the 21st century has improved the possibility of a sustainable automotive future. The present EV drivetrain run by BLDC motor has become increasingly complicated thus requiring efficient and accurate controls.

arxiv-2411-00992.title: Correlation of Correlation Networks: High-Order Interactions in the Topology of Brain Networks
arxiv-2411-00992.creator: Qiang Li, Jingyu Liu, Vince D. Calhoun
arxiv-2411-00992.description: Abstract To understand collective network behavior in the complex human brain, pairwise correlation networks alone are insufficient for capturing the high-order interactions that extend beyond pairwise interactions and play a crucial role in brain network dynamics. These interactions often reveal intricate relationships among multiple brain networks, significantly influencing cognitive processes.

arxiv-2508-19931.title: Cell-Free Massive MIMO-Based Physical-Layer Authentication Thanks: This work is a contribution by Project REASON, a UK Government funded project under the Future Open Networks Research Challenge (FONRC) sponsored by the Department of Science Innovation and Technology (DSIT). It was also supported by
arxiv-2508-19931.creator: Isabella W. G. da Silva ∗ , Zahra Mobini ∗† , Hien Quoc Ngo ∗ , and Michail Matthaiou ∗
arxiv-2508-19931.description: Abstract In this paper, we exploit the cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) architecture to design a physical-layer authentication (PLA) framework that can simultaneously authenticate multiple distributed users across the coverage area. Our proposed scheme remains effective even in the presence of active adversaries attempting impersonation attacks to disrupt the authentication process.

arxiv-2510-25405.title: Sim-to-Real Gentle Manipulation of Deformable and Fragile Objects with Stress-Guided Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2510-25405.creator: Kei Ikemura, Yifei Dong, David Blanco-Mulero, Alberta Longhini, Li Chen, Florian T. Pokorny
arxiv-2510-25405.description: Abstract Robotic manipulation of deformable and fragile objects presents significant challenges, as excessive stress can lead to irreversible damage to the object. While existing solutions rely on accurate object models or specialized sensors and grippers, this adds complexity and often lacks generalization.

arxiv-2512-05272.title: Inferring Compositional 4D Scenes without Ever Seeing One
arxiv-2512-05272.creator: Ahmet Berke Gökmen, Ajad Chhatkuli, Luc Van Gool, Danda Pani Paudel
arxiv-2512-05272.description: Abstract Scenes in the real world are often composed of several static and dynamic objects. Capturing their 4-dimensional structures, composition and spatio-temporal configuration in-the-wild, though extremely interesting, is equally hard. Therefore, existing works often focus on one object at a time, while relying on some category-specific parametric shape model for dynamic objects.

pmc-10574873.title: Dynamic Surface Properties of α-Lactalbumin Fibril Dispersions
pmc-10574873.creator: Boris Noskov, Giuseppe Loglio, Reinhard Miller, Olga Milyaeva, Maria Panaeva, Alexey Bykov, Vladimir N Uversky, Alexey L Iordanskii
pmc-10574873.description: The dynamic surface properties of aqueous dispersions of α-lactalbumin (ALA) amyloid fibrils differ noticeably from the properties of the fibril dispersions of other globular proteins. As a result, the protocol of the application of ALA fibrils to form stable foams and emulsions has to be deviate from that of other protein fibrils.

pmc-10681928.title: Integrated microbiome and metabolome analysis reveals a distinct microbial and metabolic signature in Graves' disease and hypothyroidism
pmc-10681928.creator: Wen Jiang, Ganghua Lu, Tingting Qiao, Xiaqing Yu, Qiong Luo, Junyu Tong, Suyun Fan, Li Chai, Dingwei Gao, Ru Wang, Chengwen Deng, Zhongwei Lv, Dan Li
pmc-10681928.description: Recent studies reveal that imbalanced microbiota is related to thyroid diseases. However, studies on the alterations in fecal metabolites in Graves' disease and clinical hypothyroidism patients are insufficient. Here, we identified 21 genera and 53 metabolites that were statistically significant among Graves' disease patients, hypothyroidism patients, and controls integrating microbiome and untargeted metabolome analysis.

pmc-11479533.title: Function-based risk reduction intervention for lifestyle-related disorders among inactive 40-year-old people: a pilot randomised controlled trial
pmc-11479533.creator: Lena Bornhöft, Daniel Arvidsson, Anna Bergenheim, Mats Börjesson, Jonatan Fridolfsson, Margareta Hellgren, Lena Nordeman, Maria E. H. Larsson
pmc-11479533.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background Interventions for preventing or reducing the development of lifestyle-related disorders should be investigated as these conditions are becoming increasingly prevalent and having large effects on quality of life and life expectancy globally. The aim of this pilot study was to prepare for a full-scale randomised controlled trial by evaluating the short-term changes resulting from a function-based preventive intervention aimed at lifestyle-related disorders on a small group of physically inactive 40-year-old people.

pmc-11646003.title: P120 The relationship between digital technology and sleep-wake behaviour in children aged 5-8 years
pmc-11646003.creator: C Pattinson, S Edmed, K Rossa, D Mann, J MacKenzie, L de Waal, S Smith
pmc-11646003.description: IntroductionChildren are growing up in 24-hour digital-enriched environments. Digital life may have significant impacts on a child’s 24-hour sleep-wake behaviours and wellbeing. This study aimed to explore the relationships between sleep, digital technology use, and daytime functioning in children.MethodData for this study were drawn from a pilot study investigating wearable devices in children aged 5-8 years, in their naturalistic environment.

pmc-12539090.title: Medical futility and the ethics of continuing treatment: a hermeneutic inquiry into patient and physician perspectives
pmc-12539090.creator: Ling-Lang Huang
pmc-12539090.description: BackgroundIn the context of medically futile treatment, clinical decision-making often becomes ethically and existentially fraught, especially when physicians and patients navigate the space between prolonging life and preserving its meaning. Existing shared decision-making (SDM) models often rely heavily on empirical rationality, yet overlook the ontological depth of patient experience.

pmc-12720454.title: Aberrant KIF26B expression promotes bladder cancer progression through driving NSUN2 nuclear localization
pmc-12720454.creator: Jia-Ming Wang, Hai-Yun Xie, Feng-Hao Zhang, Xuan Shu, Jin-Dan Luo, Li-Ping Xie, Jiang-Feng Li
pmc-12720454.description: Abnormal expression of kinesins has been observed in several types of cancer. The present study provided the first evidence that KIF26B could induce RNA m5C modification in bladder cancer (BCa). Detailly, KIF26B interacted with NSUN2 and recruited ubiquitinase STUB1 to promote K63-linked ubiquitination of NSUN2 at K511 site.

pmc-13094361.title: Enhancing Diagnostic Pathways for Bronchopulmonary Neuroendocrine Tumors: Assessment of the South Wales Neuroendocrine Tumor Service Transformation
pmc-13094361.creator: Arouba Imtiaz, Oliver Burbidge, Mat Jones, Robin Ghosal, Janardhan Navaratnam, Craig Dyer, Helen E. Davies, Mohid S. Khan
pmc-13094361.description: BackgroundBronchopulmonary neuroendocrine tumors (bpNETs) are uncommon lung neoplasms posing significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This study evaluates the impact of the transformation of the South Wales Neuroendocrine Cancer Service on diagnostic and management outcomes for bpNETs.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed data from patients with typical and atypical carcinoids (TC and AC) diagnosed before and after commissioned service transformation (September 2017).

pmc-13449846.title: Would the number of new cases of hereditary angioedema decrease due to declining fertility rates?
pmc-13449846.creator: Lauren Wong, Harold Kim, Mark Kuprowski
pmc-13449846.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Hereditary angioedema (HAE) is a rare, potentially life-threatening disorder caused by autosomal dominant mutations in the SERPING1 gene, leading to deficiency or dysfunction of C1 esterase inhibitor. Recent estimates of global HAE prevalence are 1.22 per 100,000 individuals. With total fertility rates (TFRs) decreasing worldwide, several developed countries are now well below the population replacement rate in an “ultra-low fertility” group. With the decrease in fertility, how rare diseases are approached should be re-examined.
